narrative.overview:
NullByte is a build log: every post is a commit in the history of something actually built, newest first, drawn as `git log --graph` at poster scale. Topics are branches. Each branch is a full-saturation rail that owns its column from the root of the log up to the newest post on it, and every post sits on its rails as a thick ink-ring node. The latest post is HEAD and is set at headline scale with its real stats; older posts follow as log rows separated by 2px ink rules.

The material is paper-flat. A pale steel ground by day and deep graphite by night, near-black (or near-white) ink, and colour reserved for the rails. Commit messages are set in a heavy, tightly tracked grotesk (Schibsted Grotesk). Monospace (Geist Mono) appears only on the data line: hashes, dates and counts. Nothing floats: there are no cards, no shadows and no rounded panels. Structure comes from ink rules and the rails themselves.

The world refuses the blog template of a hero image over a row of equal cards. It also refuses the dark-terminal costume: no neon, no glow, no monospace headlines, and no fake git history (the short hash is a display id derived from the post id).
keyCharacteristics: Pale steel ground (light) / deep graphite ground (dark), with ink rather than tinted surfaces.
Four full-saturation topic rails (vermilion, cobalt, green, violet) plus one neutral "other" rail.
Heavy, tightly tracked Schibsted Grotesk for titles; Geist Mono only for the data line.
2px ink rules as the only structure; no cards, no shadows, no rounded panels.
Rails draw up from the root to HEAD once on load; hovering a row widens its rail.
The branch switcher filters the log by topic with pure CSS, enhanced by a view transition.

rules.name: The Rail Rule
rules.body: There are exactly four topic rails and one "other" rail. Lane colour follows tag rank (the four busiest tags), not tag identity, so a tag can change colour as the log grows. A fifth colour is never added; extra topics fold into "other".

rules.name: The Named Topic Rule
rules.body: Colour never identifies a topic alone. Every swatch sits beside the topic's name in text: the branch pill names its branch, the topic link names its tag, the HEAD chip names the post's subject.

rules.name: The Ink First Rule
rules.body: Resting actions and selected states are ink. The cobalt accent appears on actions and links only as a response (hover, focus, selection), never as a resting button or link colour.

rules.name: The Data Line Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono carries data and code: hashes, dates, counts and the units that belong to them, plus code blocks and inline code. Titles, excerpts, nav, footer and topic links are always Schibsted Grotesk, even when they sit inside a mono line (topic links reset the family).

rules.name: The Small H1 Rule
rules.body: The SEO H1 stays the page's real H1, set small as the repository line. The visual focus is the HEAD title, an h2. Never promote the visual focus to h1 or drop the H1 to fix the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Class Selector Rule
rules.body: `globals.css` sets unlayered rules on `h1`–`h6`, `p` and `a` (size, weight, margin, line-height, colour, hover underline). Unlayered CSS outranks Tailwind's layered utilities, and `a:hover` outranks a single class. Style every element in this world through its own class selector, and expect to restate margin, line-height, colour and decoration that the globals would otherwise impose. The same file's global `body` and `code, pre` rules name `--font-sans` / `--font-mono`, which `@theme inline` never emits, so those declarations are dead: name `--font-display` and `--font-geist-mono` directly.

rules.name: The Flat Log Rule
rules.body: No cards, no shadows, no rounded panels. If content needs separating, use a 2px ink rule; if it needs grouping, put it on the log.

rules.name: The Hunk Rule
rules.body: A hunk line opens a section only when it tells the reader something: position, total and code count, on posts with two or more sections. A one-section post gets no hunk line and no index. The line never grows past one small mono line, and diff colours (+/− green and red) never enter the prose.

rules.name: The One Title Rule
rules.body: The commit header owns the page's only h1. A body h1 that repeats the post title is dropped; any other body h1 is demoted to h2 and becomes a hunk section.

rules.name: The Draw Once Rule
rules.body: Rails draw once, on load, from the root up to HEAD. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` they appear already drawn, and the rail, node, row, pill and button transitions are off.

rules.name: The CSS-First Filter Rule
rules.body: The branch filter is radio inputs read by `:has()` selectors and works without JavaScript. A client wrapper only adds a view transition (0.35s, same easing) where `startViewTransition` exists and reduced motion is off; otherwise the change snaps.

dos: **Do** read every colour from the `--bl-*` custom properties so the light and dark values switch together.
**Do** separate content with 2px ink rules and let the rails carry the structure.
**Do** name the topic in text next to every lane colour.
**Do** keep Geist Mono to hashes, dates and counts, with tabular numerals.
**Do** keep keyboard focus cobalt: the world remaps `--ring` to the accent, so links take the global 2px outline and the branch pill and primary button take a 3px outline.
**Do** style world elements through their own class selectors, since the global element rules outrank utilities.
**Do** honour reduced motion: no rail draw, no view transition, no rail, pill or button transitions.
**Do** keep the article's reading column calm: Article body at a 68ch measure; the world shows in the commit header, hunk lines, rules, code and links.
donts: **Don't** add cards, shadows or rounded panels to this world.
**Don't** add a fifth topic colour; fold extra topics into the "other" rail.
**Don't** set titles, excerpts, navigation or topic names in monospace.
**Don't** use neon, glows or a dark-terminal costume.
**Don't** present the short hash as a real git commit or invent history the posts don't have.
**Don't** use the cobalt accent as a resting button or link colour.
**Don't** make the visual focus the H1; the SEO H1 stays the real H1, set small.
